goal: Capture real behavior and reject failed, stale or tampered evidence.
invariants: Read-only explanation/history use canonical shared validators, preserve failed/interrupted attempts and treat provenance as an untrusted hint; technical success never supplies pending implementation acceptance.
Exclusive ignored local HTML reports remain outside canonical evidence, escape evidence text and omit raw logs unless explicit verified bounded redacted excerpts are requested.
Required failures cannot be reported successful.

Explicit independently selected pre-change policy context preserves maximum scope floors, required checks and command bindings, stronger autonomy/review/human gates and immutable proof/work bindings; missing or drifting context rejects before admission effects, while candidate-only evaluation is labeled informational for control transitions.
Before and after scenarios use identical argv.
Directory hashes cover declared source regardless of directory basename, including generated modules, excluding only exact root metadata, evidence and dependencies.
Captured timeout/output-limit results follow bounded owned-group cleanup; descendants cannot keep modifying source after stopped execution reports completion.
Every finish reserves a distinct immutable attempt before execution, preserving the original baseline and failed/interrupted attempt history.
Technical evidence supports review readiness; acceptance requires implementation review bound to the chosen canonical attempt under current policy.
Proof/review writes and current validation require whole-directory protection, explicitly distinguishing measured Git exclusion from canonical local fallback.
Excluded root dependency symlinks do not affect source-only hashes or retained proof; declared and visited source still reject symlinks.
Safely normalized root/output scope aliases reject before commands or evidence writes; prior invalid alias proof cannot qualify, while raw scope keys and legitimate nested source remain intact.
Filesystem-identical case aliases of reserved root proof scope cannot establish capture, validation, work or audit acceptance; distinct case-sensitive source entries retain freshness coverage.

Filesystem-identical source aliases and ancestor scopes retain the maximum sensitive-path and Feature Map implementation/entry-point risk floor; distinct entries and exact missing suffixes preserve source semantics.

Automatic lifecycle facts and append-only windowed observations preserve unknown metric denominators and never change proof/work risk, readiness, approval or autonomy; immutable duplicate source identities cannot inflate task/attempt counts.

Prepared proof drafts preserve exact criterion links and existing validation; missing real bug/refactor scenario identity or expected exits remains a blocker and preparation supplies no captured evidence or review.

Opt-in Git changeset proof retains explicit base/HEAD/index/raw-working inventory, covers all nonexcluded changed endpoints including deletions and renames, and rejects uncovered or later drifting state without upgrading legacy declared-only evidence.

Opt-in signed receipts verify independently selected external verifier/provider/review roots, exact immutable Git scope and retained controls; offline GitHub conformance never implies hosted assurance or production admission, and local metadata exports cannot authenticate reviews.
acceptance: Feature capture executes a configured acceptance command and validates its canonical manifest; required command failure, changed source/logs/argv or unrelated static checks prevent valid proof.
Bug start captures a failing before scenario and finish proves the same argv succeeds after correction; refactor start/finish retain passing before and after behavior.
Each finish reserves a distinct immutable attempt, retains failed/interrupted history and original baseline logs, and refuses stale or altered baseline/command bindings before execution.
R2 technical proof enables review readiness while acceptance requires actual implementation review bound to the selected attempt; failed and noncanonical attempts cannot acquire acceptance.
